messages.subject: Modifying a classpath after load
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I set my classpath using .jaddclasspath and then created an object of my
class C.
C has a method run which instantiates an instance of a user-specified class
(specified as a string) .e.g

a=.jnew(C)
a$doSomethingWith(stringnameofClass)

doSomething will try and create an object of class stringnameofclass

Unsurprisingly, since the Jar file which contains stringnameofclass was not
added to classpath before i created C, i get a "Class not found error".

I tried using JCl2 [2] to add JARs and then call
a$doSomethingWith(stringnameofClass) but to no avail.

Is there a way i solve this?

Cheers
Saptarshi

[2] https://github.com/kamranzafar/JCL

messages.subject: Re: Modifying a classpath after load
messages.body_plain:
On Feb 11, 2013, at 6:12 PM, Saptarshi Guha wrote:

> Hello,
> 
> I set my classpath using .jaddclasspath and then created an object of my class C.
> C has a method run which instantiates an instance of a user-specified class (specified as a string) .e.g
> 
> a=.jnew(C)
> a$doSomethingWith(stringnameofClass)
> 
> doSomething will try and create an object of class stringnameofclass
> 
> Unsurprisingly, since the Jar file which contains stringnameofclass was not added to classpath before i created C, i get a "Class not found error".
> 

No, that is not correct. It doesn't matter when you modify the class path, because the class loader consults the most current class path at the time of finding a new class to load. The rJava class loader specifically uses dynamic look up when loading classes, so it will work regardless of when you modify the class path (see output below).

If you have a problem with the above, it's more likely a bug in class C which may be using the wrong class loader explicitly. But for that we'd have to see your actual code.

Note that if you want to, you can always get the rJava class loader explicitly with .jclassLoader() but well-written Java applications should never need to access it directly - it should always be obtained from the class of the loaded object instead -- you can always check that it should be of the class RJavaClassLoader.

Cheers,
Simon

Illustration:

> library(rJava)
> .jinit(".")
> a=.jnew("A")
# this will fail, because I have B.class in another directory:
> a$getClass()$forName("B")
Error in .jcall("RJavaTools", "Ljava/lang/Object;", "invokeMethod", cl,  : 
  java.lang.ClassNotFoundException
# I add that directory to the class path
> .jaddClassPath("class2")
# now forName() succeeeds
> a$getClass()$forName("B")
[1] "Java-Object{class B}"



> I tried using JCl2 [2] to add JARs and then call a$doSomethingWith(stringnameofClass) but to no avail.
> 
> Is there a way i solve this?
> 
> Cheers
> Saptarshi
>

messages.subject: Re: java call r call java
messages.body_plain:
On Feb 12, 2013, at 7:51 PM, Saptarshi Guha wrote:

> Hello,
> 
> It is possible to embed R inside Java.
> 
> Q: is it possible to for an R function to call a method in a passed Java object?
> 
> i.e.
> object O of class C (in Java)
> (pseudo code)
> public void foo(){
>    Rengine.eval("myRfunction",Object2)
> }
> 
> R function
> 
> myRfunction <- function(javaObj){
> javaObj$doSomething()
> }
> 

Yes. Assuming you're using REngine, it would look something like

Object o; // Java object to pass to R

eng.assign("o", new REXPJavaReference(o));
eng.parseAndEval("myRfunction(o)");

Just make sure you have loaded and initialized rJava, e.g., eng.parseAndEval("{ library(rJava); .jinit() }"); before assigning any references.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: R_HOME in initR
messages.body_plain:
On Feb 13, 2013, at 2:49 AM, Saptarshi Guha wrote:

> Hello
> The Rengine call createEngine ends up in C, which checks for R_HOME.
> I'm in an environment where i dont have control over the environment variables and R_HOME might not be present in the environment
> 
> Would it possible to pass R_HOME to createEngine and the C code instead of using getenv would use setenv ?
> 
> If no R_HOME is provided to createEngine, createEngine could inspect System.getenv (in Java) and use the default. If none is present there, then fail
> 

There are two problems. One problem is that R_HOME is not the only environment variable that needs to be set - it's just used as a proxy to determine that the environment has beed setup correctly by R CMD. If you don't start the application using R CMD java .. then you're entirely on your own - it's not guaranteed to work as R requires the other variables as well. If you cannot use R CMD directly, then you can dump the set of variables (it differs by R version and build) and set them by other means.

The second problem is that that Rengine has no way to determine R_HOME (at least not reliably across platforms) - there are some heuristics (check on the PATH, registry on Windows etc.), but they are inherently unreliable, because what really matters is the library that has been linked into Rengine at compile time, and since that can be relocatable, there is no way to deduce R_HOME reliably. Therefore you always need some way to tell Rengine how to find its R and R_HOME is the way. At one point we used to have code in JRI that allows you to set environment variables, but it caused portability issues so it has been removed. If you have some other mechanism in mind to specify the R location, let me know, but I fear that we'll have to re-visit the portability issues we had by using setenv in 
 C and as I said it's just one of several variables that needs to be set, so you'd have to pass them all.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am having some teething problems embedding JRI, though I think it
can be easily solved. That solution however escapes me.

A bit of background. I am the author of RHIPE which embeds R in
Hadoop, allowing the user to write mapreduce programs from R.  That is
not the trickiest bit, the trickiest bit is getting R to work on the
nodes.

In our cluster (at Mozilla), R is not present on the nodes and never
will be. The solution around this is [3] a small bit of code that
takes the R distribution, (lib64/R/ downwards) and the users R_LIBS,
creates a tar.gz file and sends it to th nodes (using Hadoops
DisributedCache).

The current approach is:

1) The zip archive is unzipped on the local nodes
1) Create environment variables, R_HOME, R_DOC_DIR, R_INCLUDE_DIR ,
LD_LIBRARY_PATH
pointing to this zip archive
3) Launch R

This works. It is really convenient, since i can have multiple R
distributions, update packages, recreate this archive and away we
go. No need to install packages on 55 nodes or request sysadmin to do
things

JRI
===

So, i want to move to JRI. I've had some very good experience with
JRI - e.g I could read 1.5 GB across 2000 R objects from the HDFS into
R in 18 seconds. Pretty nice.

I wish to embed JRI in my Java job. For some reason java.library.path
is not reflecting my jri source. So instead before i create Rengine
instance, I load the jri.so file and set ignore.ule to 'yes'. Also i
have set R_HOME, LD_LIBRARY_PATH etc Thus JRI loads successfully and
then i get the following issues ([2])

I'm not sure how this is possible. For jri.so to load, libR.so must be
present (i removed libR.so and jri.so would not load) Also
Rf_allocS4Objec is present in librR.so, so i'm not sure why this cant
be found?


Do you have some paths i could investigate?
Cheers
Saptarshi

buildingR <-
function(excludeLibs=c(),exclude=NULL,iterate=TRUE,verbose=TRUE,nameof="Rfolder-test"){
  library(Rhipe)
  rhinit()
  local({
    tfolder <- sprintf("%s/Rdist",tempdir())
    ## delete folder if it exists!
    dir.create(tfolder)
    execu <- if ("package:Rhipe" %in% search()) rhoptions()$RhipeMapReduce
else sprintf("/home/%s/software/R_LIBS/Rhipe/bin/RhipeMapReduce",USER)
    getLB <- function(n){
      a <- system(sprintf("ldd  %s",n),intern=TRUE)
      b <- lapply(strsplit(a,"=>"), function(r) if (length(r)>=2) r[2] else
NULL)
      b <- strsplit(unlist(b)," ")
      b <- unlist(lapply(b,"[[",2))
      b <- unique(unlist( sapply(b, function(r) if(nchar(r)>1) r else
NULL)))
      names(b) <- NULL
      if(verbose){
        cat(sprintf("\n%s depends on:\n",n))
        cat(paste(b,sep=":",collapse=" "))
        cat(sprintf("\n---------------\n"))
      }
      b
    }
    b <- getLB(execu)
    ## b <- unique(b[!grepl("(libc.so)",b)])
    for(x in b) {
      cat(sprintf("Copying %s to %s\n",x,tfolder))
      file.copy(x,tfolder) ##copies the linked .so files
    }
    file.copy(execu,tfolder,overwrite=TRUE)  ## copies the RHIPE C engine
    file.copy(R.home(),tfolder,recursive=TRUE)
    ## R_LIBS
    x <- Sys.getenv("R_LIBS")
    if(nchar(x)>1){
      for(y in list.files(x,full.names=TRUE)){
        if(all( sapply(excludeLibs,function(h) !grepl(h,y))))
          file.copy(y,sprintf("%s/R/library/",tfolder), recursive=TRUE)
      }
      allfiles <- list.files(x,full.names=TRUE,rec=TRUE)
      allsofiles <- allfiles[grepl(".so$",allfiles)]
      alldeps <- sort(unique(unlist(sapply(allsofiles, getLB))))
      id <- 1
      if(iterate){
        while(TRUE){
          message(sprintf("iteration %s", id))
          alldeps2 <- sort(unique(unlist(sapply(alldeps, getLB))))
          newones <- sum(!(alldeps2 %in% alldeps))
          if(newones>0){
            message(sprintf("There were %s additions(total=%s), iterating
till this becomes zero", length(newones), length(alldeps2)))
            id=id+1
            alldeps=alldeps2
          }else  break
        }
      }
      if(!is.null(exclude)) alldeps <- alldeps[!grepl(exclude,alldeps)]
      for(x in alldeps) {
        cat(sprintf("Copying %s to %s\n",x,tfolder))
        file.copy(x,tfolder) ##copies the linked .so files
      }
    }
  })
  cat(sprintf("Building a gzipped tar archive at
%s/%s.tar.gz\n",tempdir(),nameof))
  system (sprintf("tar z --create --file=%s/%s.tar.gz -C %s/Rdist
.",tempdir(),nameof, tempdir()))
  cat(sprintf("Copying gzipped tar archive to HDFS (see %s) in user
folder\n",sprintf("%s.tar.gz",nameof)))
  if ("package:Rhipe" %in% search())
rhput(sprintf("%s/%s.tar.gz",tempdir(),nameof),sprintf("/user/%s/",USER))

Two suggestions here:

a) (optional) try doing it the other way round - i.e. setup the R environment as you do and then set java.library.path property in Java to include the JRI directory. Then load and start JRI. I'm not 100% sure if the loader you are using will honor the change but it should. If it doesn't you could use the RJavaClassLoader explicitly - it automatically detects JRI libraries if they are present so no additional settings are needed.

b) the package errors suggest that you have R version mismatch -- i.e. you may be loading packages from other place than you think - they require more recent version than what you are using. Check .libPaths() in the R instance to verify that. If in doubt, nuke all packages and re-install them.

Cheers,
Simon

messages.subject: Re: TLS/QAP with Java Rserve client
messages.body_plain:
> From: Joël Kuiper <me at joelkuiper.eu>
> Date: February 21, 2013 3:40:25 AM EST
> To: stats-rosuda-devel-bounces at listserv.uni-augsburg.de
> Subject: TLS/QAP with Java Rserve client
> 
> 
> Quick question: Is TLS/QAP from the 1.7.0 package supported by the
> Java Rserve client? I couldn't find any documentation on how to use
> this.
> 

No, it is not supported. Currently the only client supporting TLS is the RSclient.

However, given that Java has SSL support it is probably not hard to add to the Java client - I'll have a look and report on it unless someone else already has a patch.

Cheers,
Simon
